title: Launch-gate administration source record
description: The canonical source record for ONE administration of the launch gate defined by launch-gate-pre-specifications.md (v2.0 and later). This file is the machine annex of the instrument's section 5. The Markdown administration report is GENERATED from a record conforming to this schema and is never parsed back as authority. No field here adopts, accepts, or approves anything (VIS-4). The record carries no final verdict: the verdict is computed by scripts/validate_launch_administration.py from the rows, and a `final_verdict` key is rejected by additionalProperties rather than compared, so a claimed verdict can never be the thing a reader trusts.

schema_version.description: The version of THIS schema the record was authored against. A record naming a version the validator does not implement is rejected, never read on a best-effort basis.

administration_kind.description: instrument section 2's full-vs-delta rule. Only a `full` administration can support a gate decision; a `delta` record is lawful for steering and is rejected as gate evidence.

formal.description: True when this administration is offered as one a launch decision may rely on. A formal administration must be full, fresh-context, and disclose its model family (instrument section 2).

path.description: Repository-relative path of the instrument as committed at repository_commit.

version.description: The instrument's effective_version at repository_commit, e.g. `v2.0`.

sha256.description: sha256 of the instrument file as committed at repository_commit.

parameter_block_sha256.description: sha256 of the instrument's section 8 parameter block as bound for this administration, computed from the committed instrument.

repository_commit.description: The named commit. Every citation in this record must exist at it; evidence quoted from any other version is void (instrument section 2).

launch_target.description: Verbatim from the parameter block's LAUNCH_TARGET, or its first sentence. Compared whitespace-normalised against the committed instrument.

deferred_waves.description: The parameter block's DEFERRED_WAVES. May be empty; an empty array asserts that none are deferred.

model_family.description: The reviewer's model family, or `human`. F5's disclosure lives here.

same_family_as_corpus_authors.description: instrument section 2: a family-constant administration measures agreement as much as convergence and must say so. Declared, never inferred.

deviations.description: Anything added, missing, or unreadable relative to the fixed materials list. An empty array asserts there were none.

operationalization_notes.description: Every judgment call made interpreting a question. An empty array asserts none were made.

e3.description: E3's credibility protocol (instrument section 3): concepts enumerated, each traced to the governing shape artifact, then the reopen list. An empty reopen list without the trace table is Unknown, never Met.

reopen_items.description: Vision- or shape-level questions authoring the first spec would force reopening. Non-empty means E3 is not Met and no READY verdict is lawful.

e4.description: E4's fixed cases (parameter block E4_CASES), classified from their text alone, then compared against the routing authority. Agreement is computed, never authored.

routing_authority.description: The parameter block's E4_ROUTING_AUTHORITY path, as read at repository_commit.

case_index.description: 1-based index into E4_CASES, in the parameter block's own order.

case_text.description: The case quoted verbatim from the parameter block. Compared against the committed instrument, so a paraphrased case cannot carry a verdict.

reviewer_classification.description: Two-valued by instrument section 3 — the reviewer always classifies.

routing_authority_says.description: `silent` when no rule of the routing authority covers the statement; a silent case counts as neither agreement nor disagreement.

needed_by_launch_target.description: True when the launch target needs this case routed. Silence over such a case is a finding in its own right.

owner_deferrals.description: Deferrals granted by the owner, each claimed only by citation. A reviewer's own wording is not a deferral (instrument section 4).

decision_citation.description: A repository path existing at repository_commit, or an SDR-n identifier. P-n names the pending queue and grants nothing.

bounded_reduction_plan.description: Required for an F2 deferral by instrument section 4: maximum new meta-artifacts, artifacts to retire, stop condition.

deferred_wave_findings.description: Defects living only in a deferred wave's candidate semantics. Any scoped row requires at least one entry here (instrument section 4).

blocking_conditions_met.description: Which of instrument section 4's five blocking conditions the defect meets. A scoped verdict is lawful only when this is empty.

reopened_findings.description: Findings previously recorded resolved that recurred. An empty array asserts zero; the array's absence is an error, never an implicit zero (VIS-2).

pilot_recurrence_check.description: The parameter block's PILOT_RECURRENCE_CHECK, performed and recorded rather than silently skippable.

g1.description: The completeness critic. G1 yields no Met/Not-met verdict and never blocks, but an administration missing it is incomplete and cannot support a gate decision (instrument section 3).

critic_answer.description: What readiness dimension could this project fail that no question in the series would catch?

falsification_summary.description: What the reviewer tried to break across the administration and could not.

prior_record.description: The immediately preceding administration this one is compared against for the trend row, or null when this record opens the log.

question_id.description: A roster identifier: A1-A6, B1-B5, C1-C7, D1-D4, E1 with its five sub-rows, E2-E6, F1-F6. G1 is a section, never a row.

question_digest.description: sha256 of the question's verbatim text as administered, or the literal `instrument-bound` when the record binds identity through the instrument digest instead. A verdict rendered against a paraphrased question is void (instrument section 2).

verdict.description: The closed vocabulary. `Unknown` carries its reason in unknown_reason; the rendered form is Unknown(reason). Nothing else is lawful — no `Partially met`, no `Met with caveats`.

launch_scope.description: Authored independently of the verdict word and cross-checked against it: `deferred-wave-only` is lawful with the scoped verdict and with no other, so one typo cannot launder a defect out of scope.

evidence.description: Required for Met. Every entry is commit-anchored to repository_commit.

locator.description: Line, range, or stable identifier (a clause ID, a heading).

counterexample.description: Required for either Not met form: the artifact and passage that fails, or the sweep with its denominator. Null when the verdict is not a Not met.

unknown_reason.description: The parenthetical of Unknown(reason). Null unless the verdict is Unknown.

unknown_settlement.description: What evidence would settle it. Required for Unknown; null otherwise.

falsification_attempt.description: What the reviewer tried in order to break this question or its verdict. A question surviving no genuine attempt has no credible verdict (instrument section 2).
